THE TILING. Sphere centres spaced R apart (not 2R) so neighbours overlap and share atoms --
which is what the proposal requires for a change in one sphere to be felt in the next.
MULT is how many spheres each atom lands in; it multiplies the work, it is not free.
R  atoms/sph     spheres   mult  pairs/sph   TOTAL pairs  vs cell list
THE COMPARISON THAT MATTERS. The last column is sphere tiling against a plain cell list at
the SAME cutoff, which computes each pair once and is exact within it. Tiling is strictly more
work for the same physics, because overlap re-evaluates shared pairs. A decomposition only
repays that when each sphere does a nonlinear local SOLVE whose cost is superlinear in m --
a minimisation or an SCF. NEXUS's per-sphere operation is a pairwise SUM, so there is nothing
to amortise and the overlap is pure overhead.
THAT COLUMN IS THE SAME 4.2x AT EVERY RADIUS, AND THAT IS NOT A COINCIDENCE IN THE DATA:
total tiled pairs = N*mult*(m-1)/2 and cell-list pairs = N*(m-1)/2, so the ratio is exactly the
overlap multiplicity (4/3)pi and the measured density cancels out. It is a geometric fact about
covering space with overlapping balls, not a measurement -- reported as such so it is not read
as an empirical finding that happened to come out constant.
WALL CLOCK, from a measured pair rate on this machine.

R   total pairs   core-seconds   core-years
AND THAT IS FOR ONE ENERGY EVALUATION OF ONE STATIC STRUCTURE.
It is worth being exact about what it does and does not buy, because the proposal's stated
goal was to avoid brute-force MD. MD's cost is not the per-step spatial sum -- it is the
10^6-10^9 STEPS. Sphere tiling is a way of organising one step. It does not touch the
timescale, so it cannot substitute for dynamics; it can only make a single snapshot cheaper,
and the column above shows it makes it dearer than a cell list.
